headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH TRUCE EXPIRES NOVEMBER 10 — No Renewal Signal From Beijing as Deadline Risks Cascading Into Jan 2027 Trade Window
snippet: Beijing's one-year suspension of expanded rare earth export controls — covering dysprosium, terbium, and other critical magnet materials — expires November 10, 2026, with no public renewal announcement from China's MOFCOM as of mid-October. Analysts identify three possible outcomes: extending the pause, selectively reimposing some controls, or fully restoring the October 2025 measures with extraterritorial reach; the deadline falls nine days before the reported January 2027 US-China trade truce expiry, creating a cascading risk for Western rare earth developers and defense supply chains.

headline: PALADIN SHARES DIVE 7.8% — Langer Heinrich Uranium Output Falls 19% as Plant Recovery Drops to 85% and Costs Surge to $61.60/lb
snippet: Paladin Energy (ASX: PDN) reported Q1 FY2027 production of 1.00 million pounds of U3O8 at Langer Heinrich in Namibia — down 19% quarter-on-quarter — as plant recovery fell to 85% from 90% and unit production costs rose to US$61.60/lb from US$51.60/lb, driven by a planned July maintenance shutdown and harder ore in the upper J-pit benches. The ASX uranium producer maintained FY2027 guidance of 5.1–5.6 million pounds and expects H2 improvement as drilling transitions to higher-grade ore feed; shares fell 7.8% to A$7.40 in early trading.

headline: LUCA MINING COMPLETES C$211M FINANCING — US$290M Cozamin Copper-Silver Mine Buy from Capstone Copper Targets Q4 2026 Close
snippet: Luca Mining (TSX-V: LUCA) completed C$211 million in subscription receipt financings — led by National Bank Financial's C$155 million bought deal with concurrent participation from Wheaton Precious Metals and Taurus — to fund its US$290 million acquisition of Capstone Copper's Cozamin polymetallic mine in Zacatecas, Mexico. Proceeds are held in escrow pending Mexican antitrust approval and TSXV sign-off; on closing, Cozamin would transform Luca into one of Mexico's leading polymetallic producers with approximately 30 million pounds of copper equivalent annually.

headline: JAGUAR URANIUM FILES LAGUNA SALADA MAIDEN RESOURCE — 4.2M Lbs U3O8 Indicated Plus 10.1M Lbs Inferred With 31M Lbs Vanadium in Patagonia
snippet: Jaguar Uranium (NYSE American: JAGU) filed its maiden NI 43-101/S-K 1300 resource estimate for the Laguna Salada uranium-vanadium project in Chubut Province, Argentina: 21.1 million tonnes at 119 ppm U3O8 equivalent (4.2 million lbs U3O8 + 31.1 million lbs V2O5 indicated) plus 34.0 million tonnes at 170 ppm inferred (10.1 million lbs U3O8 + 57.3 million lbs V2O5). Only 4.3% of the 210,284-hectare property has been drilled; the company recommends an immediate $1.93 million expansion program.

headline: ERDENE'S ZUUN MOD PEA: $745M AFTER-TAX NPV — 34-Year Open-Pit Molybdenum-Copper Mine in Mongolia Rises to $2B NPV at Spot Prices
snippet: A preliminary economic assessment for Erdene Resource Development's (TSX: ERD) Zuun Mod Molybdenum-Copper Project in Mongolia returned an after-tax NPV of US$745 million and 16.1% IRR at US$25/lb molybdenum and US$5/lb copper — rising to US$2.0 billion NPV at current spot prices. The study models a 34-year open-pit producing approximately 20 million lbs of molybdenum and 28 million lbs of copper annually with US$687 million upfront capex; drilling begins late October 2026 to upgrade a resource that remains 74% inferred ahead of a prefeasibility study.

headline: APOGEE MINERALS EXPANDS KNIFE LAKE COPPER PROJECT — Adjacent Eagle Plains Claims Acquired to Consolidate Saskatchewan Copper-Cobalt Land Package
snippet: Apogee Minerals (TSX-V) acquired adjacent mineral claims from Eagle Plains Resources to expand its Knife Lake Copper Project in the Trans-Hudson Corridor of Saskatchewan, consolidating the land package around the historical copper-cobalt deposit and closing a potential exploration gap on strike. The expansion opens untested extensions of known copper-cobalt mineralization in a district benefiting from renewed critical metals interest as the US-China supply chain dispute elevates North American project valuations.

headline: GOLDSEEK: Gold Must Hold $4,100 and Silver $58 — $4,500 and $66 Are the Breakout Triggers Ahead of October 27-28 FOMC
snippet: A GoldSeek technical analysis identifies $4,100 gold and $58 silver as the critical support levels whose breach would confirm a deeper correction from the February 2026 record peaks, while $4,500 and $66 are the upside triggers required to resume the primary bull trend. The analysis recommends defined trigger-based entry points rather than trying to call the bottom, framing the October 27–28 FOMC meeting as the near-term binary catalyst that resolves whether the current range-bound consolidation breaks higher or lower.

headline: BHP AVERTS ESCONDIDA STRIKE — Copper Falls to $14,342 as World's Largest Mine Secures Labour Deal and LME Stocks Edge Higher
snippet: Benchmark three-month copper on the LME fell 0.4% to $14,342/t as BHP reached a tentative labour agreement with Escondida workers — averting a strike threat at the world's largest copper mine — while LME warehouse stocks edged higher. Chile's Cochilco simultaneously lowered its 2026 copper output forecast 2.6% to 5.27 million tonnes; the near-term supply concern relief contrasts with the structural picture of a 17-year average mine development pipeline and long-dated deficit forecasts underpinning junior copper developer valuations.

headline: GOLDSEEK ASIAN METALS UPDATE: Gold and Silver Steadily Declining From Feb Records — October FOMC the Key Reset Point
snippet: GoldSeek's October 19 Asian metals market update notes that gold and silver have been in a sustained multi-month retreat from their February 2026 record highs — gold's $4,873 and silver's near-$70 — with both metals entering the final week before the October 27-28 FOMC at technically precarious levels. The update flags Brent crude above $111/barrel as a factor amplifying the inflation-versus-rate-hike tension that is simultaneously capping gold's safe-haven bid and raising the cost of holding it.
